clue.text: Wrapped gift, being soft on Clare, perhaps

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the name may be given in some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone notes a wrapped present arriving, perhaps a tender one for a woman named Clare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes Clare look like an example of a woman, but it signals rearranging her name; 'on' places the soft marking first in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a package done up in paper, the usual form of a gift under the tree.

clue.text: Stages which will be packed at Christmas

definitions.meaning: to stage a play is to put it on, as a verb meaning puts on or shows

definitions.text: which will be packed at Christmas
definitions.meaning: gifts wrapped and packed into sacks and stockings for the festive season

explanation.definitionFit: To present a show is to stage it, and gifts given at Christmas are its traditional packages.

clue.text: They lead the way in the present transport system

definitions.text: They lead the way in the present transport system

parts.words: They lead the way in the present transport system
parts.note: reads like a remark about public transport, but means the animals pulling the sleigh that carries Christmas gifts

explanation.surface: A remark about who heads up the current public transport network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like 'current' but means gifts: the system delivering presents is Santa's sleigh, and its leaders are the animals harnessed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's sleigh is pulled by a team of antlered animals, so they head the gift-delivery system.

clue.text: These trees may be obtained from Wilhelmstrasse

indicators.note: the run of letters can be pulled straight out of the street name, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Some trees can be found along a famous Berlin street.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilhelmstrasse was the Berlin street of government ministries; the letters sit in wilhELMStrasse.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a tall deciduous tree, so the plural names a group of such trees.

clue.text: It's suspended just before Christmas

parts.note: sounds like something halted or postponed, but means the item hung up by the fireplace on Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: Something is put on hold in the run-up to the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' suggests cancelled or halted; here it simply means hung up, as a child's sock is on Christmas Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas stocking is hung by the fireplace on Christmas Eve for Santa to fill.

clue.text: They gave original Christmas presents

parts.note: reads as praise for inventive gift-givers, but points to the gold, frankincense and myrrh brought to the infant Jesus

explanation.surface: Praise for some people whose gifts were unusually inventive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' seems to mean inventive, but means the very first: the Magi's gifts in the nativity story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi of the nativity story brought gold, frankincense and myrrh, the first Christmas gifts.

clue.text: Trim tree finally with attractive result

parts.note: to trim something is to cut it

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word tree is used

explanation.surface: Pruning a tree back has given it a pleasing look.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means charming or pretty, a near synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Where Jesus lived is setting up a king

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up means the word is raised from bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: Lear is the legendary British king of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A biblical land is said to be installing a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' reverses the king upwards, as this is a down entry; the king is Shakespeare's tragic monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus lived in Galilee and Judea, lands making up the modern state named here.

clue.text: About the end of December, reached Santa's base

indicators.note: about means the second phrase's letters are placed around the first

parts.note: reached a place means got to it

indicators.note: the end of means only the final letter of December is taken

explanation.surface: Late in December someone arrived at Father Christmas's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts GOT TO round R, the last letter of December.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is the decorated cave in a department store where children visit Santa.

clue.text: Game in crackers is a mystery

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go mad and are reordered

explanation.surface: A puzzle game is found inside the Christmas crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the festive novelties but means crazy, rearranging GAME IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or something baffling, a direct synonym of a mystery.

clue.text: One that talks one round to see Handel's Messiah?

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A speaker brings a friend along to hear Handel's famous work.
explanation.definitionFit: Messiah is a celebrated example of a large-scale sacred choral work of this kind, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Like Idle Jack in pantomime? Definitely not

definitions.meaning: Idle Jack is a lazy pantomime character in Dick Whittington, doing no work at all
a firm refusal, a flat no

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone doing no work, and is also an idiom for a flat refusal.

clue.text: Dead drunk, providing old stories

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man found dead drunk is the source of ancient tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic collection of Norse myths and legendary tales.

clue.text: Christmastide presents of theatre seats

definitions.meaning: Christmas ... are gifts or tips given at Christmas, especially to tradespeople
private compartments of seating at the side of a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: Christmas boxes are festive tips, and a theatre's private seating compartments share the name.

clue.text: Party includes a number in religious group

indicators.note: includes means the first word's letters hold the second inside

parts.note: a set is a group of people, a social party or clique
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A political party has a number of members from a religious faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts C inside SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a breakaway faction within a religion, so a religious group.

clue.text: By start of evening a Christmas tree may be lit up

parts.note: taken as written
the fir is the evergreen traditionally used as a Christmas tree

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of evening is used

explanation.surface: By nightfall the decorated tree might be blazing with lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire means burning or ablaze, so figuratively lit up.

clue.text: What may be decked, when sun rises, will

indicators.note: in a down entry the letter for sun climbs to the top of the word

parts.note: the carol says deck the halls with boughs of holly

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what gets decorated once the sun comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when sun rises' moves S from the end of HALLS to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The auxiliary verb expressing future or determination, a synonym of will.

clue.text: Famous play in its second week on January 5th?

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's comedy of Viola and Orsino

definitions.text: in its second week on January 5th?
definitions.meaning: the evening of 5 January ends the twelve days of Christmas, well into the festival's second week

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy shares its name with the eve of Epiphany, the last of the twelve days of Christmas.

clue.text: Tiptoe in craftily to get round robin

indicators.note: craftily means slyly worked, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone creeps in slyly to collect a Christmas newsletter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' rearranges TIPTOE IN. 'round robin' looks like the Christmas letter or bird but is the signed appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a document signed by many people making a joint request.

clue.text: Run out of decorations in packets, perhaps

indicators.note: out of means the letter is taken away from the following word

parts.note: streamers are paper decorations hung at parties
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone has used up all their festive paper decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes R out of STREAMERS. Packets were mail steamers on regular routes.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet was a passenger and mail ship, usually steam-driven, so an example of the type.

clue.text: Rip off celebrant out to be the first to decorate the tree in UK

definitions.text: the first to decorate the tree in UK

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order and reset

explanation.surface: A con artist cheats a clergyman, who turns out to be a pioneer of festive decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RIP and CELEBRANT; 'off' just joins them. Queen Victoria's husband popularised the German Christmas tree in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's consort popularised the decorated Christmas tree in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Frozen hanger-on

parts.note: reads as a cold, unwelcome follower, but means a spike of ice dangling from a roof

explanation.surface: A chilly hanger-on who will not go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanger-on' usually means a sycophant; here it is literally something that hangs on, made of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is frozen water hanging from an edge, literally a frozen thing that hangs.

clue.text: A Christmas present drawer

parts.note: sounds like a drawer for storing gifts, but means one of the team that draws the sleigh full of presents

explanation.surface: A drawer in which Christmas gifts are stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture but means one who pulls: one of Santa's named animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancer is one of Santa's named reindeer, who pull the sleigh laden with gifts.

clue.text: Pass round a traditional New Year's gift

indicators.note: round means the first word's letters go around the second

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone hands round a customary present at New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts COL round A. In Scottish first-footing a guest brings a lump of fuel for luck.
explanation.definitionFit: In first-footing, the first visitor of the year brings a lump of this fuel for luck.

clue.text: I had conducted the carollers, perhaps, but became lazy

parts.note: contracted to I'd
led means conducted, as one might lead a group of carol singers

explanation.surface: Someone once led the carol singers but has since grown idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to be lazy and do nothing, so the past tense means became lazy or loafed.

clue.text: Christmas spirit always surrounds her

indicators.note: surrounds means the outer words enclose the letters of the name

explanation.surface: The festive spirit always envelops a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits in spiRIT Always, held by the surrounding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rita is a woman's name, so it can stand for any her.

clue.text: It may hold needles on the tree — but only as a present

definitions.text: It may hold needles on the tree — but only as a present

parts.words: It may hold needles on the tree — but only as a present
parts.note: suggests a branch holding pine needles, but means a small sewing case hung on the tree as a gift

explanation.surface: Something that holds needles on the Christmas tree, though only as a wrapped gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needles' looks like pine needles; they are sewing needles in a case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for sewing needles, a classic small gift.

clue.text: Watch punch initially trickle away

parts.note: to watch is to see

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of punch is used

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the festive punch bowl as it leaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To seep is to ooze slowly out, a close synonym of trickle away.

clue.text: Drink — it's the end of the bird

definitions.text: it's the end of the bird
definitions.meaning: the tail of a cockerel, its rear end

explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a mixed drink, and read literally it is the tail of a cock.

clue.text: Ingredients relating to cold mince pie

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: mince means chop up, so the letters are chopped and reordered

explanation.surface: Notes about the components of a chilled mince pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks part of the festive pie but rearranges PIE into IPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe lists the ingredients and method for a dish, so it stands for the ingredients loosely.

clue.text: Presents for ladies are out with some circles

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: rings are circles

explanation.surface: Gifts for women are on sale with some round items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ARE into EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Earrings are jewellery worn by women, a common gift for them.

clue.text: Fancies outsize tree inside

indicators.note: inside means the tree's letters go within the other piece

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
the pine is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone fancies an extra-large tree indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancies' looks like a noun but is the verb, thinks or supposes; OS is the clothing-label code for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or express a view, close to fancies in the sense supposes.
